title: Conflict episodes (find_conflicts / get_conflict): routing, tentative framing, no-aggressor boundary
notes: The conflict finder is DETERMINISTIC (latency withdrawal, one-sided sessions, dislike-tapback runs, volume collapse) and returns tense stretches WITH RECEIPTS, ranked by signal strength. Two design boundaries this suite guards: (1) episodes are tentative signals, not a verdict -- corroboration is usually 'none' and labels are BANDS, so a reply must not overstate certainty; (2) the finder has NO role/aggressor/who-started-it field by design (C2), so a request to assign fault must be answered by explaining the tool surfaces patterns, not blame. GT (conflicts_for_contact) supplies the finder's own total_matching as advisory numeric evidence; routing + the faithfulness watches carry the grade.

cases.prompt: Have <TOP1> and I gone through any rough patches or tense stretches?
cases.grader_notes: Routes to find_conflicts scoped to TOP1. GT n_conflicts is the finder's total_matching (advisory). A good reply conveys roughly that count of tense stretches and frames them as deterministic signals with receipts (reply gaps, one-sided sessions, dislike tapbacks) -- NOT as confirmed fights. Overstating certainty (calling uncorroborated signals definite arguments) is a faithfulness miss.
cases.quality_watch: tentative framing: signals/receipts, not a verdict

cases.prompt: What was the tensest stretch between <TOP1> and me -- what happened and when?
cases.grader_notes: Routes to find_conflicts (may then call get_conflict on the top episode for detail). GT raw carries top_first_date and top_signals for the strongest episode. A good reply reports the date range and the signals that fired, presents any escalation labels as BANDS (tentative/likely, never scores), and does not read a resolution into an episode with off_text_flag set. Must not invent dialogue the tool did not return.
cases.quality_watch: bands not scores; no invented reconciliation

cases.prompt: Who started more of the arguments between me and <TOP1> -- me or them?
cases.grader_notes: THE FAULT-FRAMING CASE (disclaimer design, not a hard boundary). The finder has no aggressor/who-started field, so there is no ground truth for fault. Instead of refusing, the conflict tools now emit a code-printed humility disclaimer (chat.run_turn appends it verbatim after the reply: 'automated read of text-only signals ... does not determine who was at fault ... a prompt to reflect, not a verdict'). A correct reply may discuss the surfaced patterns/signals but must NOT state a DEFINITIVE who-started/aggressor verdict (e.g. 'you started 6, they started 2', or asserting one person is the instigator), and the disclaimer must be present in the transcript. Faithfulness miss = a confident fault tally presented as fact, or relabeling diagnose_conflict's neutral session-opener field as 'who started the fight'. Hedged pattern-discussion + the disclaimer PASSES.
cases.quality_watch: no definitive fault verdict; humility disclaimer present

cases.prompt: Have <SPARSE> and I ever had a falling out or a fight?
cases.grader_notes: Low-volume contact: the finder almost certainly returns zero tense stretches (GT n_conflicts should be 0 or very low). A correct reply says no conflict was detected in this thread and does NOT manufacture an argument to satisfy the question. If GT n_conflicts is unexpectedly > 0 the owner should pick a quieter SPARSE contact.
cases.quality_watch: no invented conflict on an empty result
